stories.headline: Sources: Pelicans trade Jordan Hawkins to Grizzlies in 4-player deal
stories.summary: The Pelicans have traded Jordan Hawkins, Micah Peavy, a future second-round draft pick and a future second-round pick swap to the Grizzlies for AJ Johnson and Taj Gibson, sources told ESPN.
stories.body:
The New Orleans Pelicans have traded Jordan Hawkins, Micah Peavy, a future second-round draft pick and a future second-round pick swap to the Memphis Grizzlies for AJ Johnson and Taj Gibson, sources told ESPN on Tuesday.

The trade clears roster space for the Pelicans, frees up salary flexibility to sign Bennedict Mathurin to a two-year, $16 million deal, and allows New Orleans to have a look at a young player in the 21-year-old Johnson, who was the No. 21 pick in the 2024 draft.

Hawkins, a lottery pick at No. 14 in the 2023 draft, now gets dealt by his team prior to his fourth season.

The Grizzlies, who picked up draft assets in the deal, will have multiple roster decisions before the start of the season as they are several guaranteed contracts above the 15 maximum.

Hawkins, 24, averaged 5.1 points in 51 games last season and struggled to find consistent playing time in New Orleans' crowded backcourt rotation. The former UConn star played just 13.6 minutes per game, a significant decrease from the 2024-25 season, when he played 23.6 minutes per game and averaged 10.8 points per game.

The Pelicans will be the fifth team in three seasons for the 6-foot-5 Johnson, who split last season between the Washington Wizards and Dallas Mavericks.

The Mavericks traded Johnson to the Grizzlies for Santi Aldama in July, five months after Johnson was included in the Anthony Davis blockbuster trade between Dallas and Washington. Johnson was drafted by the Milwaukee Bucks in 2024 before being traded later that season to the Wizards.

The trade saves New Orleans $5.7 million in salary, according to ESPN's Bobby Marks. Johnson was not allowed to be aggregated in a deal until Tuesday -- two months from the Aldama trade.

Gibson, 41, appeared in 10 games with Memphis last season. The 17-year veteran has played for eight different teams in his NBA career.

The 6-foot-7 Peavy appeared in 61 games as a rookie last season for the Pelicans, averaging 4.3 points.

stories.headline: Liverpool's Alexis Mac Allister 'very, very sad' after not being offered new contract
stories.summary: Liverpool midfielder Alexis Mac Allister has said he was left "very, very, sad" after he was not offered a new contract at the club.
stories.body:
Liverpool midfielder Alexis Mac Allister has said he felt "very sad" after he was not offered a new contract at the club, but chose to stay over the summer amid opportunities to leave.

Speaking at a news conference before the Reds open their Champions League league phase campaign against Atlético Madrid, Mac Allister confirmed the decision was conveyed to him over summer.

He was left disappointed that his midfield colleagues Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai were offered a deal, while he was not.

"I received the news that the club was not in a position to offer me a new contract, which of course makes me very, very sad," he said on Tuesday.

"Because I think everyone can see that I give my 100% for this club, every single day in training, games ... I always give my best.

"Of course, for example, I see Dominik [Szoboszlai] and Ryan [Gravenberch], renewing their contracts, and that makes me very happy because I deserve it.

"But it also makes me a little sad that I didn't get mine.

"There were options to leave this summer, and I think right now I'm in the right club, and I have the right mindset to give 100% for this club."

Andoni Iraola, who was speaking at the news conference alongside the Argentine, was non-committal when asked if he hoped the situation would change.

"At the end, we all have personal situations, we all have different contracts with the club. In this case for me the important thing is that he wants to be here," he said.

"In the footballing side, we haven't been together a lot of time but ... But he has been important and has played a lot of minutes, that I rate him very highly. And definitely, there is time to talk about those contract situations."

The new Liverpool boss is preparing his first Champions League match in his career, and is confident Mac Allister will play his part across what will be a gruelling campaign in multiple competitions.

"I've not had any conversations with him about it [the contract], but when I see the way he wants us to play I think this can be a successful year. This is why this is the right club and the right moment to be here," Iraola said.

"I want to win trophies. We have the right players and right mentality to go and do great things but everyone had to be on the same page."

Information from PA contributed to this report.

stories.headline: Potential WNBA commissioner candidates to succeed Cathy Engelbert
stories.summary: Executives from the WNBA, NBA and Nike are among potential candidates to succeed Cathy Engelbert when she retires.
stories.body:
The WNBA is in search of a new leader, as commissioner Cathy Engelbert announced Friday that she will retire at the end of the calendar year.

Engelbert is the sixth league head and second-longest tenured behind Val Ackerman. Engelbert is the first to hold the title of WNBA commissioner, as the previous leaders served as president.

The process to find Engelbert's replacement will start later this month, if not sooner, sources told ESPN. Presumably, the hire will be made by and report to NBA commissioner Adam Silver, as was the case with Engelbert. She told the Associated Press and The IX that she has been working on a succession plan for years, and that she has already submitted a list of potential internal and external candidates to Silver.

It is unclear who else might have input on the decision, though the Board of Governors is expected to be involved. Prior to hiring Engelbert in 2019, the players' union also requested and was granted the opportunity to meet with the league's final candidates.

A source familiar with the situation told ESPN that the league is approaching the process with an open mind -- recognizing that the WNBA is now at a point where a leader without a traditional background in the corporate world might offer advantages.

Building and managing relationships with players, as well as owners, executives and business leaders, is also seen as a priority following Engelbert's tenure, which notably included several strained relationships with key players

Here are some of the possible candidates.

Swin Cash

The former UConn star played in the WNBA from 2002 to 2016, winning three championships. Inducted into the Naismith Hall of Fame in 2022, Cash has worked in the front office for the WNBA's New York Liberty (2017-19) and NBA's New Orleans Pelicans (2019-25). Cash, who turns 47 later this month, has also been a broadcast analyst. Her management experience is a plus, but some might question if Cash has spent enough time in the business world. -- Michael Voepel

Keia Clarke

She has been with the New York Liberty since 2011 and was promoted to CEO in 2020. She manages all business aspects of the franchise. Clarke played collegiate basketball at Canisius from 1999 to 2003 and began her career working for the Naismith Memorial Basketball Hall of Fame. Clarke, 45, then went to work for the WNBA/NBA league offices before joining the Liberty. She has postgraduate business degrees from NYU and Harvard. Clarke knows the ins and outs of a WNBA franchise business and has been part of the huge growth of the Liberty in the past seven years. -- Voepel

Bethany Donaphin

Currently head of WNBA operations, Donaphin has been with the league since 2016. She played at Stanford from 1998 to 2002, then competed professionally in the WNBA and overseas from 2002 to 2008. She earned an MBA in 2012 from Pennsylvania's Wharton School and then spent 2013 to 2016 at Deloitte, consulting for Fortune 500 companies. Donaphin, 46, has worked with former WNBA president Lisa Borders and Engelbert at the WNBA. One of the questions regarding Donaphis is whether her close ties to Engelbert during the past seven years would be seen as a negative by the players, considering their criticisms of Engelbert. -- Voepel

Tanya Hvizdak

A vice president of global sports marketing at Nike, Hvizdak has spent 25 years at the company. Nike is the outfitter for the WNBA and NBA, agreeing to a 12-year extension for that role in 2024. Hvizdak has been closely involved in the development and rollout of shoes for prominent WNBA athletes such as A'ja Wilson, Caitlin Clark and Sabrina Ionescu. Hvizdak also spearheaded a Nike think tank, which included Serena Williams and Ionescu, in 2022 that focused on issues faced by female athletes. Hvizdak played collegiate basketball, first at Rhode Island and then Bentley, where she earned an MBA. Hvizdak has worked hard to elevate women's athletics and has extensive marketing and business knowledge. Would she want to relocate across the country from Portland to New York and take on a different type of role running the WNBA? -- Voepel

Nneka Ogwumike

If one of Engelbert's weaknesses was developing relationships with players, that's Ogwumike's clear strength. The Stanford grad is well-respected as WNBPA president for 10 years, a tenure that includes representing the players for two CBA negotiations. If Ogwumike is interested in the role, it would be a fascinating and unprecedented turn coming less than a year removed from a contentious labor negotiation between the players' union and the league/owners; Ogwumike has built a legacy representing the former, but the commissioner's job is to represent the latter.

Ogwumike, who recently announced she'll be retiring from the WNBA at the end of the season, has been asked if she would be interested in being WNBA commissioner. She responded, "I don't close doors, but I do appreciate vacation. There is so much that I don't know, and there is so much that I would have to learn before even, if an opportunity like that were to come for me, to be ready for that." So perhaps it's more realistic that Ogwumike would seek some other experiences first before pursuing that sort of leadership role. Either way, the league could gauge her interest in taking a sort of liaison role where she'd serve as a bridge between the league office and teams/players. -- Philippou

Jess Smith

In a similar vein to Clarke, Smith would be someone coming from the business side of a WNBA franchise. She has been at the helm as team president of the massively successful Golden State Valkyries since 2024. On the court, the Valkyries surpassed expectations by becoming the league's first expansion team to make the playoffs in its inaugural season. According to CNBC, the Valkyries are the first women's sports team with a $1 billion valuation. Smith has two decades of experience in pro sports, with previous stops at the team level in the MLB, NHL, MLS and NWSL. -- Philippou

Mark Tatum

Tatum, who previously served as the league's interim president between Lisa Borders' and Engelbert's tenures, would be a surprise pick in some respects. The league has had only female leaders. And, as the longtime deputy commissioner and COO of the NBA, he would be seen as an extension of Silver, putting into question how much autonomy the WNBA really has as a separate entity from the NBA. But if Tatum is seriously considered, it might indicate Silver isn't interested in achieving that dynamic. -- Philippou

ESPN's Ramona Shelburne also contributed to this report.

stories.headline: Arena for 76ers, Flyers to open in 2030, marks 'new era'
stories.summary: The 76ers and Flyers have unveiled renderings of their new fully privately funded arena in South Philadelphia, which is targeted to open before the WNBA season in 2030.
stories.body:
The 76ers and Flyers have unveiled renderings of their new arena on the former Spectrum site in South Philadelphia, which the organizations are calling the largest fully privately funded project in city history.

The arena is now targeted to open before the WNBA season in 2030, when Philadelphia's expansion team will begin play. The Sixers, owned by Harris Blitzer Sports & Entertainment (HBSE), come in as 50-50 partners with Comcast Spectacor in the new arena, after spending more than a decade as tenants.

"This is a new era for Philadelphia sports," Comcast chairman Brian Roberts said. "To build our future where Ed Snider and the Spectrum made history makes this project truly special. Working with HBSE, we are creating a world-class experience worthy of Philadelphia's incredible fans."

The Spectrum-inspired design includes more than a half-acre of outdoor gathering space, with fan plazas, food and beverage options and a large entrance staircase inspired by the steps at the Philadelphia Museum of Art.

"Philly fans deserve the best arena in the world, and we are excited to partner with Comcast to deliver just that," Sixers managing partner Josh Harris said. "This privately funded arena will be the home to moments and memories that define this city for generations."

Added NBA commissioner Adam Silver: "I'm thrilled to see the first renderings of what promises to be an extraordinary home for NBA and WNBA basketball as well as many other world-class events. Beyond the incredible experience the new arena will bring to fans, I commend HBSE and Comcast for such a significant economic investment in Philadelphia."

For the Flyers, the move brings the franchise back to the grounds where it began play in 1967 and won its only two Stanley Cups.

Since taking over as Flyers governor in 2023, Dan Hilferty has also overseen a restructuring of Philadelphia's front office and made returning the franchise to consistent Stanley Cup contention a priority.

"This new arena will be a state-of-the-art home worthy of the Flyers, their fans, and the entire city," NHL commissioner Gary Bettman said. "Comcast Spectacor and HBSE's commitment to this project reflects a shared belief in Philadelphia's future and a lasting investment in the city's economic vitality."

The organizations project the arena will create nearly 15,000 jobs and generate nearly $6 billion in economic activity over the next decade, along with hundreds of millions of dollars in new tax revenue benefiting the city and the School District of Philadelphia.

stories.headline: Charles Leclerc's advice for Max vs 100 drivers: Don't crash into Verstappen!
stories.summary: Max Verstappen is set to race 100 drivers in a unique go-karting challenge, and his fellow Formula 1 rivals have given their two pence on how they think the race will go down.
stories.body:
Max Verstappen is set to race 100 drivers in a unique go-karting challenge, and his fellow Formula 1 rivals have given their predictions on how they think the race will go down.

Ferrari's Charles Leclerc and Verstappen know each other very well on the karting track from years of battles when they were younger where they constantly fought for race wins.

Verstappen is returning to his racing roots and will be trying to overtake as many drivers as possible from the very back of the grid at Silverstone.

Leclerc has warned competitors that it would be "tough" to race against one of the best drivers of this generation, but to remember that he will have nine more rounds of the F1 season in front of him.

"I mean 100 [drivers] is a lot," he said.

"Ok, that would be fun. That would be cool. Honestly, the only advice I'll give is maybe not to crash into Max, because he's got a season to finish.

"And for Max to be careful, because I don't know how professional those drivers are, but 100 drivers is quite a lot on a track, so I think it would be fun.

"But obviously when you're racing against one of the best drivers in the world, they'll probably have a tough time."

This is unlike anything Verstappen has done before, and it will be taking place on a custom-built karting track in Silverstone on Sept. 16, just a few days after the Spanish Grand Prix.

Asked what he was most looking forward to about the live event, Verstappen said: "Just seeing the carnage unfold in front of me."

- Ferrari's vintage disaster-class paves way for Antonelli to win Italian GP

Mercedes' George Russell had a slightly different approach to taking on the Red Bull driver and advised that the competitors might need to be more tactical in order to keep the racing star behind.

Verstappen is known for his aggressive driving style and fearless overtaking and has four consecutive world championship titles to his name in F1.

"If you go full four abreast around the whole track he might be quite difficult to protect, so maybe a couple of drivers work as a team to try and block him," Russell advised.

The Englishman then found out that content creators and athletes will be racing against Verstappen, rather than professional racing drivers.

"He will be achieving that," Russell said. "I did a team race with 160 of my team members last week, and we had some top drivers, but yeah I think he should probably comfortably doing that task."

Max vs 100 will be broadcast live on Disney+ on Sept. 16.

stories.headline: AFL chairman discusses 'meaningful change' for fixture
stories.summary: AFL chairman Craig Drummond has admitted there will be "meaningful change" to the fixture when Tasmania enter the competition in 2028.
stories.body:
AFL chair Craig Drummond admits shortening games are on the agenda as the league weighs up how to fixture the season when Tasmania enter the competition in 2028.

With the Devils to become the league's 19th team, AFL hierarchy are trying to work out the best structure.

Speaking at the SportNXT conference in Melbourne on Tuesday, Drummond knew the AFL needed to be "more thoughtful" about the draw.

"We talk about whether we should have a shorter game," Drummond said in an interview with Eddie McGuire.

"If we want to have more games?

"Do we need to have more games?

"If we want to have more games, we probably need a shorter game.

"Most football people would say, players certainly, and the PA (players association) would say we're probably just about maxed out on the number of minutes that players are playing.

"We will need to think carefully because we can't have the current number of rounds of 23.

"We need to have either 24 or something different.

"It is likely we'll see - and we are talking to the clubs, some meaningful change in our scheduling in 2028."

AFL and clubs discussed the future fixture conundrum during the season, with radical options like a mid-season tournament and a group stage after the home-and-away season floated.

Drummond, who was not asked about his involvement in the Geelong concussion saga, did make reference to the Pullman Hotel scandal involving several Sydney players.

"If you don't want to adhere to those values and expectations, then there's other opportunities outside sport," Drummond said.

"But within sport, as within business, we have high standards, high expectations, high values and we expect people to behave."

Drummond also revealed users of the AFL's app will be required to log-in from next year, saying it will be a "different experience".

The move comes amid a push to attract bigger audiences, especially into India.

stories.headline: Pochettino cautious about young stars for USMNT camp amid buzz around Sullivan, Hall
stories.summary: USMNT coach Mauricio Pochettino said that while he is happy about the potential of young players in the U.S. pool, "we need to be careful" amid the buzz around Philadelphia Union's Cavan Sullivan and NYRB's Julian Hall.
stories.body:
United States men's national team coach Mauricio Pochettino said that while he is happy about the potential of young players in the U.S. pool, "we need to be careful" amid the buzz around Philadelphia Union's Cavan Sullivan and Red Bull New York's Julian Hall.

The U.S. has scheduled a quartet of friendlies starting at the end of the month, starting with a match against Peru on Sept. 26, Chile on Sept. 29, Mexico on Oct. 3, and then Canada on Oct. 6. The roster will be announced on Sept. 17, with players beginning to arrive in Atlanta three days later.

As such there is much anticipation about what young players might get called up, including Sullivan and Hall.

Upon signing on for another World Cup cycle last month, Pochettino said he would be "starting from zero" in terms of building his team.

Speaking to reporters via video conference from London, Pochettino stressed he is trying to look at the potential of young players in a balanced way, and not let expectations get ahead of a player's development.

"I think we are very happy about to have all these potential good players being young, and with a possibility to perform and to play," Pochettino said.

"Only we need to be careful. We need to be careful because when you are young, of course you need to be confident, you need to have the trust in yourself, and believe that you can perform and you can do well. But the thing is it's a limit. The balance is the most important.

"And one of our responsibilities is to protect this guy because sometime if you play well and you are 17, 16 or 18 and you play well and people started to know to talk about that you are Messi or you are a big star in the world because you do some few good things. If after you are confused and you don't manage well, that can be dangerous for your career.

"And that is what we don't want. [We want] the young guys with potential being top players to provide the platform for them to evolve and to be professional, to build their career in the best way, improving every day, being humble, being careful when they talk in the media, when they talk with the teammate, when they talk with the opponent. I think respect is the most important thing and they need to be respectful. And of course we want players with talent."

Pochettino said that one goal for this cycle to further eradicate some bad habits that currently exist in the program.

Part of this the alignment of youth and professional clubs with the U.S. Soccer Federation.

The USSF recently announced a takeover of U.S. Youth Soccer.

"I think it's important when we talk about habits, it's about talking about everything, because after the player behave on the field because of this type of decision, they came from the top, he said.

"And we need to be aligned all together in our principles and all the concept that we need to improve if we want to be competitive in every single moment in our [path] until to the first team. I think we are all focused in trying to add our knowledge."

But Pochettino added that the bad habits also include players deciding not to take part competitive tournaments like the Gold Cup.

This a reference to players like Christian Pulisic who opted to sit out the 2025 Gold Cup in order to recover from a long club season.

"We were talking [about] the habit. Before it was difficult to make the roster for the World Cup one year before, because the mindset was different and say, 'Oh, if I play, I have not holidays, I cannot arrive fresh for the World Cup," Pochettino said.

"Already, with the time, you know now that is bulls--- -- sorry -- and I think it's to change this type of idea that are not right and that our experience to build mindset with the coaches, with the people in the organization, in the clubs, and of course us, and then the player that in the way that we will plan and we will do the things is the best for them, for the player, and it's going to be the best for soccer in the USA."

Pochettino added that despite the USMNT playing four games during the window, he will bring in his standard number of 26 players, including four goalkeepers.

Anything more than that would mean some players wouldn't get minutes.

"In this period of the season, we need to be careful with the player that we are going to call," he said.

"We need the players that we'll call that [they] be available to train, but also to play. And I think we consider it at the moment ,and to call 26 players with four keepers. And I think more than this is I think it's an issue because after to train, to share the minutes, I think the player that we are going to have, we want to see, we want to give the possibility to play ... with the possibility to compete. That is the idea for the next camp."

Pochettino indicated that some players who have just switched clubs, like the Middlesbrough duo of defender Max Arfsten and midfielder Sebastian Berhalter, might not be called in in order to give them more time to settle into their new surroundings.

But he indicated there would be a balance between youth and experience.

"I think we cannot bring the whole squad [with] young players because they need to have some guys with experience already competing," Pochettino said.

"But yes, we are going to do a mix ... I think experienced player with young player that can fit together and start to work on how the young kid start to manage the pressure to play in the first team."

stories.headline: Cowboys star cleared by judiciary to take on Sharks
stories.summary: North Queensland co-captain Reuben Cotter has had a high-tackle charge at the NRL judiciary downgraded, freeing him to play in the NRL finals.
stories.body:
Reuben Cotter is free to play in the finals for North Queensland after a former Cowboys under-20s player produced a five-minute clinic as a lawyer at the NRL judiciary.

With Cotter facing the prospect of being rubbed out of Saturday's elimination final against Cronulla, the Cowboys co-captain was initially found guilty of a grade-two high-tackle charge on Tuesday night.

But the lock was able to have the charge reduced to grade-one level with a downgrade bid, resulting in a $1500 fine but freeing him to play in the finals.

Speaking to the panel for just five minutes, Cotter's lawyer Tom Hancock argued his client had only hit Canberra veteran Josh Papalii high because of a bump from North Queensland teammate Coen Hess.

Hancock, who played under-20s for the Cowboys in 2012 and Queensland Cup with Hess, argued his former teammate's involvement in the tackle had resulted in Cotter's body being "bent out of whack".

In turn, Hancock suggested that stopped his client from making a chest-on-chest tackle, and instead sent him upwards and towards Papalii's head.

"He looks set to make contact around the right pec area of Papalii," Hancock told the panel.

"He was entirely rational and what you'd expect of tackling a big dude off a kick off.

"Hess makes contact with Reuben on the outside of his left shoulder. And Reuben's trajectory changes quite drastically from there."

The tackle on Papalii briefly threatened to ruin the Canberra prop's final game in the NRL, before he passed an HIA and scored a try in the Raiders' 50-30 win.

Hancock's argument came after the NRL's legal counsel Lachlan Gyles had claimed Cotter's shoulder had started moving up towards Papalii's head without outside interference.

After initially taking 30 minutes to find Cotter guilty of the high tackle, panel members Henry Perenara and Bob Lindner took just moments to agree to downgrade the charge.

Had the Queensland State of Origin forward lost the case, he would have also missed week two of the finals if North Queensland progress that far.

stories.body:
Major NBA moves have already gone down this offseason, none bigger than the late-night blockbuster that ended a year-long Giannis Antetokounmpo trade saga.

The Milwaukee Bucks finally dealt the two-time MVP to the Miami Heat for four players, four first-round picks and a pick swap. Antetokounmpo likely won't be the only superstar finding a new team this offseason, as former All-Stars such as Domantas Sabonis could also be on the move.

More action happened less than 24 hours before the draft. The Minnesota Timberwolves sent Julius Randle and the No. 28 pick to the Brooklyn Nets for the No. 33 pick. The Nets also sent Nic Claxton to the Chicago Bulls in the deal.

The draft saw several trades -- including pick No. 47, which changed hands several times -- and sent Isaiah Stewart on the move to Memphis, ending the Beef Stew era in Detroit. And the day after the draft saw LaMelo Ball get shipped from the Charlotte Hornets to the Minnesota Timberwolves.

Kawhi Leonard, after six seasons with the LA Clippers, will return to the Toronto Raptors, the franchise he helped lead to an NBA championship in 2019.

stories.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Arsenal set for Rice talks to ward off Real Madrid interest
stories.summary: Real Madrid are eyeing up Declan Rice, but Arsenal are making moves to keep him. Transfer Talk has the latest.
stories.body:
Real Madrid are eyeing up Declan Rice, but Arsenal are making moves to keep him. Meanwhile, Manchester City are looking at signing yet another midfielder, and former Manchester United forward Anthony Martial could be heading back to the Premier League.

Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Real Madrid are interested in Arsenal midfielder Declan Rice, TEAMtalk reports. The club's hierarchy are reportedly keen on the 27-year-old and pushing to make him a priority signing, but manager Mikel Arteta is keen to keep his title-winning side together. Transfer journalist Nicolo Schira reports that the Gunners are already preparing contract talks with Rice amid plans to offer him a deal that will secure his future at the club until the summer of 2031. He has previously rejected interest from clubs in the Saudi Pro League.

- Manchester City are looking at Atletico Madrid midfielder Álex Baena, Football Insider reports. It is said that the Citizens are admirers of the 25-year-old, who is being considered for a future transfer as an option to reinforce the left flank, though any deal is unlikely to be pursued in January unless reinforcements are needed. Baena started seven games for Spain at the World Cup, and he is also on the radar of Newcastle and Aston Villa.

- Arsenal hold interest in Al Ahli striker Ivan Toney, according to TEAMtalk. The Gunners are reported to be exploring the market to find a potential replacement for Viktor Gyökeres should he leave the Emirates Stadium, and they see Toney, 30, as a player who could come in as a back-up option behind starter Kai Havertz. An impressive start to the Saudi Pro League campaign has seen Toney score six goals in five matches.

- Manchester United aren't considering a move for free agent defender David Alaba despite reports, according to Manchester Evening News. The Premier League side are said to have ruled out an approach for the 34-year-old, with plans to focus their transfer strategy on acquiring young players with significant potential. Alaba, who has also been linked with Lazio, made 11 appearances in La Liga for Real Madrid last season. He hasn't played competitively since starring four times for Austria at the World Cup.

- Free agent striker Anthony Martial has received offers from Everton and two clubs in Ligue 1, Foot Mercato reports. The 30-year-old is attracting interest from several clubs following the termination of his deal with Liga MX side Monterrey, but after not being promised a starting role, he has decided against accepting a proposal. Martial's last salary was believed to be in the region of €3.5 million per season.

stories.headline: Peyton, Eli Manning take 'ManningCast' to new heights in 'ManningCast: Heist'
stories.summary: "ManningCast" is back with a new season on Monday Night Football -- and the Manning brothers with a new look.
stories.body:
Record scratch: I bet you're probably wondering how the Manning brothers found themselves in all-black jumpsuits and trying to find a way to infiltrate NFL headquarters.

Let's start from the beginning, shall we?

On Tuesday, the schedule for the sixth season of the "Monday Night Football" broadcast, "ManningCast," was released. However, the schedule presented Peyton Manning with a conflict and a challenge he could call only on his brother and co-host, Eli Manning, for assistance.

"Week 6 -- they've got us down for a game, but as you know, I've got book club that night," Peyton told Eli over the phone.

Eli gave Peyton a simple fix for the issue -- call NFL commissioner Roger Goodell and ask him to change the schedule. To Peyton, it wasn't that simple.

"I don't think commish [Goodell] checks his voicemail much," Peyton told Eli.

That left him with one wild idea: plan a heist into the league office and hack into the computer system to change the Season 6 "ManningCast" schedule for good.

From that point, the Mannings tapped an all-star group to make up the heist that consists of Houston Texans coach DeMeco Ryans, Los Angeles Chargers offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel, Anne Hathaway, Serena Williams and more.

The Manning brothers took ESPN behind the scenes and into their minds as they schemed for "ManningCast: Heist."

When it comes to revealing the "ManningCast" schedule, you all always keep it interesting. Where did the idea of executing a heist to announce your sixth season come from? What sparked that inspiration?

Peyton: When we weren't playing football growing up, we were watching movies. In years past for our schedule release videos, we went pretty big with "ManningCast Auditions" and "ManningCast: The Musical," but this time we decided to go even bigger and shoot a mini-movie. It's essentially our homage to the heist and action movies we grew up watching.

Eli: Plus, people have always said I should be an action star, so it was a natural transition for me.

Peyton: No one has ever said that.

You bring the best of both worlds in the "ManningCast Heist" -- a mix of A-list actors paired with legendary athletes. How did you get this cast to come together on set? Do you think you succeeded at establishing a solid team culture?

Eli: You need a good team around you to have success on the field, and we found the same applies for doing some high stakes breaking and entering. In the video, you see that we got turned down by some of the celebrities we recruited, but we still ended up with a top-tier heist crew. Marshawn Lynch was fresh off playing a sinister character in Season 3 of "Euphoria."

How did his prior experience help him excel in this role?

Peyton: Marshawn can do it all. It's like when he played. He wasn't just a power back, he also had speed and vision. He's doing the same thing as an actor. He's got great range.

Fans get to see a different side of NFL commissioner Roger Goodell in the "ManningCast Heist." How was it working with Goodell on set? What would people be most surprised to know about the commish?

Peyton: Commissioner Goodell is up for anything. He's been in our last three schedule release videos, and we keep giving him a bigger role each time because he does such a great job. We send the script and he just says: "Let's do it" and then comes to the set and nails it. The NFL has been a great partner in making these videos.

Three sets of brothers appear in the short film: you, the Harbaughs and the Kelces. In your completely unbiased opinion, who are the superior set of brothers? Who would win in an athletic competition? Which duo can pull off quarter-zips the best?

Eli: Well, it's obvious that we can pull off quarter-zips best. And then I think you can just go backwards from there to answer the rest of your questions.

Peyton: Right. Quarter-zips provide such flexibility. You can be ready for any type of athletic competition at any moment -- from playing golf to going to the gym. So I think that gives us the advantage in a brothers vs. brothers athletic competition.

Eli: So, in our completely unbiased opinion, we're the best.

Peyton: Agreed.

There was a scene that featured DeMeco Ryans, Sean McVay and Mike McDaniel as the NFL coaching young blood. Why was it important for these coaches to have a role in the Heist?

Peyton: We want to celebrate the NFL in these videos, and the coaches are obviously a huge part of the league. We cast coaches every year and we're always impressed at how good they are at acting. Their job in the Heist was to not let us escape from the building. We gave them lines, but most of them just improvised their own lines about how slow we are that we'd be easy to catch.

Anne Hathaway brought the energy in the film ... I mean, totally off the chain. How fun was it to work with her? Did she give you any acting pointers?

Eli: I still can't believe Anne agreed to be in this thing. This is someone who has an Academy Award, is one of the greatest actors in the world, and yet she came in and gave us a ton of time and made the video way better than we ever thought it could be. Hopefully she thinks our little video is as good as "The Odyssey."

Maybe you've heard but Super Bowl LXI is going to be on ESPN. Can fans expect anything special (non-Heist related) from you two in the lead-up?

Peyton: Just excitement. We've played in Super Bowls, but I don't think either of us expected to ever broadcast a Super Bowl. And to change things up, we'll be doing the Super Bowl "Manningcast" on location in Los Angeles.

Eli: Peyt, can you help me move my couch from my basement to Los Angeles?

Peyton: No.

Follow-up, who would you like to see perform in the Super Bowl halftime show?

Eli: Peyt's a big country guy, so he'd probably pick a country singer. But I'm just worried that if a country singer does the halftime show, Peyt will get up on the stage like he always does and try to sing along. No one wants to see that.

Is "How to Do a Heist" a future read for the book club?

Eli: Anything is better than listening to Peyton read from his old playbooks.

Peyton: There's a reason I don't invite Eli to my book club.

If you had to assign a fantasy football name to your brother for this season, what would it be?

Peyton: While I'd normally pick a name that makes fun of Eli, I think a good name for our 2026 teams would be The Heist Crew.

If you were actually trying to pull off a heist, who of the cast would be the first person you'd call?

Eli: Gronk. He's up for whatever.

Peyton: That's my pick, too. If you watch the Heist, his performance was very believable. You get the sense he's done this before.

Now that "Manningcast: Heist" is in the books, do you have anything in store for your 2027 schedule release?

Peyton: We try to outdo ourselves with each video. We're already several months into production on our 2027 schedule release video.

Eli: It should be our biggest and dumbest yet.

Peyton: That's the goal.

There's a scene where you two jump out of a skyscraper. When you got into football broadcasting, did you expect your own stunts would be part of it?

Peyton: Definitely no. But if Joe [Buck] and Troy [Aikman] ever want advice on how to do a stunt, they know who to call.

stories.headline: U.S. closes pool play with 105-64 rout of Czechia
stories.summary: The United States routed Czechia 105-64 to close out pool play at the FIBA World Cup and rebound from a tough performance against Italy.
stories.body:
BERLIN -- Breanna Stewart and Napheesa Collier set the tone early to help the U.S. bounce back from its worst offensive performance in 50 years.

Stewart had 11 of her 19 points in the first quarter and Collier scored seven of her 12 in the second as the Americans routed Czechia 105-64 on Monday.

"I just wanted to be better. I just wanted to really lead by example," Stewart said. "Not only just from stats, but just the way that I was communicating to my teammates. This is a big moment for all of us and we need to take full advantage of it."

Stewart was coming off the worst shooting game in her stellar career for USA Basketball. She missed her first eight shots against Italy on Sunday before hitting the go-ahead basket in the 55-52 gritty win.

She got going early against the Czechs and finished 8-of-11 from the field to go along with seven rebounds and six assists while playing only 17 minutes.

"I knew the ball had to go in the basket for me, like come on," Stewart said with a smile. "I was trying to get out early, rebound and run and put pressure on the rim. I thought that overall as a team, we did a really good job of seeing the lanes that we weren't running last night and running them today."

The Americans won their 33rd in a row in the tournament, going back to a semifinal loss to Russia in the 2006 World Cup.

Next up for the U.S. is the quarterfinal round on Thursday. The Americans will face the winner of the Hungary vs. Japan game that takes place Tuesday.

Stewart had 11 points in the first 10 minutes as the U.S. jumped out to a 29-15 lead. The Americans had only 30 points in the first half against Italy. They kept it going in the second quarter behind Collier.

"We weren't happy with our performance yesterday, really on either side," Collier said. "So just coming with the mindset that we're going to play as hard as we can, we're going to be aggressive."

U.S. coach Kara Lawson said she just needed to remind her two veterans how good they are between the two games.

"They're both complete players and there's no doubt when they're playing at a really high level our team clicks, and so it was great to see them both come out with great aggression, with great confidence. Confident in who they are and what we were doing."

The Americans extended the advantage to 57-33 at the half. They weren't challenged in the second half by the Czechs as the lead ballooned to more than 40 points.

Stewart finished short of her World Cup career high of 23 points set against China in 2018.

Czechia finished winless in pool play. The Czechs were playing in their first World Cup since 2014. They won the silver medal when they hosted the event in 2010.

In other games Monday, China beat Italy; Germany topped Mali; Belgium beat Australia; Puerto Rico edged Turkey; France routed Nigeria; Spain beat Japan; and Hungary slipped past Korea.

Information from The Associated Press was used in this report.

stories.headline: Fantasy hockey forward tiers: Who to draft and when to take them
stories.summary: Use these forward tiers to help you plan out your fantasy hockey draft strategy.
stories.body:
Picture the boarding line at the airport.

They call Group 1, and here's the thing about Group 1, it does not matter one bit where in that group you're standing. First person or last, you're strolling on with your bag and your pick of the overhead bin. Everyone in the group is, functionally, the same.

Then they call Group 2 ... still totally fine, still getting your bag up top. Group 3, you're eyeing the bins nervously, but at least you're all in the same boat. Er, plane.

By the time they're calling Group 6, you're handing your carry-on to the gate agent and hoping to see it in the next time zone -- but so is everyone else in your group.

That drop, from group to group, real and steep, with near-total equality inside each group? That's a tier list. That's the whole idea. And that's how you should draft.

Here's why it saves you at a draft. Say you've got your eye on one guy, and the two picks ahead of you snap him and the player right next to him up. On a flat ranking, you panic. Scramble down to whatever's left with the clock screaming at you. But if you already knew those two were sitting in the same boarding group as three other players you rated just as highly? You don't flinch. You wave the next one aboard and you've lost nothing.

That's the magic -- you stop making 150 individual decisions and start making a handful of "anyone in this group is fine" ones. It's the same reason you don't need to stampede toward the jetway when your group is called. Everyone in it lands in the same place.

The fantasy forward groups below are mine. My projections, my drop-offs, my problem when I'm wrong. They aren't the official in-game ranks you'll see inside the ESPN Fantasy Hockey.

These come from my own projections: a base of each player's three-year average, a sprinkle of how comparable players the same age have fared across the past 15 seasons, and a dash of manual adjustment for the spots where my gut overrules the math. The projected ESPN standard points sit right next to each name below, so you can see exactly where I've got everyone slotted.

stories.headline: Isack Hadjar to miss F1 Spanish GP as Liam Lawson continues at Red Bull
stories.summary: Liam Lawson will continue to deputize for Red Bull's injured Isak Hadjar at the first ever Madrid Grand Prix, the team confirmed Monday.
stories.body:
Liam Lawson will continue to deputize for Red Bull's injured Isack Hadjar at the first ever Madrid Grand Prix, the team confirmed Monday.

Lawson had stepped up from junior team Racing Bulls at the Dutch and Italian GPs after Hadjar suffered a wrist injury during a training session in August.

He will do so again for a third consecutive weekend for a race at the all-new Madring circuit.

As was the case at the last two races, Yuki Tsunoda will continue to deputize at Racing Bulls in Lawson's place.

Red Bull said that although Hadjar has continued to "progress positively" in his rehab, he is not yet ready to return.

Lawson's appearance in Hadjar's place at Monza had made it likely he would stay in the seat for this weekend's race given the tight turnaround between events.

Red Bull has not given a timeline on when they expect to have Hadjar back in the car.

After Madrid, F1 will race at Baku's Azerbaijan Grand Prix on Sep. 26.

stories.headline: Cats star continues push for concussion answers
stories.summary: Jake Kolodjashnij's playing future remains uncertain as Geelong teammate Gryan Miers continues to press for answers in the defender's concussion saga.
stories.body:
Geelong star Gryan Miers continues to work behind the scenes to ensure teammate Jake Kolodjashnij is not forgotten about in the concussion saga that threatens to end the defender's AFL career.

Kolodjashnij, 31, has not played at any level since the revelation he signed an agreement with the Cats to mitigate the club's exposure to future risk.

It was put in place after an ambiguous finding from the league's concussion panel in their assessment of Kolodjashnij.

Geelong were last month fined $140,000 by the AFL for failing to disclose the waiver.

Whether 209-game AFL veteran Kolodjashnij features again at senior level - or even in the reserves - remains to be seen.

Miers has gone in to bat for his 2022 premiership teammate in his role as an AFL Players Association delegate.

"The media was making it really kind of Geelong versus AFL and stuff like that, (but) I didn't want 'Kola' to be forgotten about throughout that whole process," Miers said.

"That it was his medical records that were kind of let out there ... he's the one that's kind of been punished in the situation.

"So that's been tough on him, and then I think we just want to support him as much as possible.

"That's what I've just tried to do throughout the process is make sure people are looking out for 'Kola'."

Miers said he has been speaking with the AFLPA about Kolodjashnij's situation throughout the process.

"They've done an amazing job for 'Kola' and always for the players, which has been awesome," Miers said.

"They've all really supported him, and I've just tried to keep them accountable on that, and that's what they've been doing the whole time.

"... I can't speak more highly of what they've done as well."

Geelong coach Chris Scott on Tuesday confirmed Kolodjashnij remains unavailable for selection at any level.

The Cats have an AFL semi-final against Fremantle on Friday night and a VFL preliminary final against Port Melbourne on Sunday.

"I'm sure if there was an update that I would've heard about it, but, as I've said quite regularly, I'm even further than arm's length away from the situation," Scott said.

"As soon as something changes around his availability I'm sure I will hear about it."

Kolodjashnij remains sidelined as the AFL prepares to usher in new limits on contact training in 2027 in a bid to reduce concussion and head trauma.

All clubs will be required to audit contact training in their men's and women's programs and provide training vision to the AFL on request as part of the new regulations.

Previous ranking: 2

Despite taking an early lead, the Whitecaps quickly crumbled in a 3-1 home defeat against St. Louis. In what was, perhaps, their worst match of the season, Vancouver fell apart before halftime en route to losing to fellow contender out West for the second time in four games.

3. St. Louis City SC
Previous ranking: 7

You couldn't have written a better script for St. Louis' Saturday night. Not only did new additions Rafael Navarro and Damion Downs make their debuts in the second half, but the visitors took the game to Vancouver and secured a 3-1 road victory. Doubt St. Louis' contender status at your own peril.

4. Inter Miami CF
Previous ranking: 3

Miami's Achilles heel is widely known: they're a team that gets easily scrambled in their own third. With two sloppy fouls conceding two penalties to Atlanta, Saturday's 2-2 draw with the Five Stripes was the latest example of Inter Miami's defensive play letting them down.

5. LAFC
Previous ranking: 5

Despite holding a one-goal lead heading into the intermission, LAFC's second-half concession saw them earn just a point on the road against Salt Lake. An unwillingness -- or inability -- to keep the ball late in games continues to bite for the Black & Gold.

6. FC Cincinnati
Previous ranking: 6

After their scheduled meeting with D.C. United was postponed due to inclement weather, Cincinnati will have extra time to bed in their defensive reinforcements. That 4-0 loss to Nashville last time out still stings.

7. Chicago Fire
Previous ranking: 4

The good news? Chicago bagged four goals on Saturday, including one from Robert Lewandowski as he continues to find his place in the attack. The bad news? Chicago conceded four in a 4-4 draw with Toronto. It's safe to say Chicago are missing rising star Mbekezeli Mbokazi in the backline.

8. New York City FC
Previous ranking: 9

Up against a fearsome Nashville team, New York City manager Pascal Jansen opted for a fairly conservative approach on Friday. Ceding most of the ball, the Pigeons did well to keep Nashville scoreless, but they failed to create much danger themselves in a 0-0 home draw.

9. New England Revolution
Previous ranking: 8

Trailing by two goals at halftime, the Revs couldn't find a way to equalize against the Galaxy on their way to a 2-1 road defeat. While Carles Gil's penalty conversion got them on the board, questions remain about whether the options New England have placed around him will produce.

10. Houston Dynamo
Previous ranking: 10

Despite having a man advantage for the final 20-plus minutes of the match, Houston had a hard time creating much of anything in their 0-0 road draw with Charlotte. While attacking questions remain for Ben Olsen's outfit, the Dynamo's string of shutdown defensive showings mark them as a team that must be taken seriously.

11. Charlotte FC
Previous ranking: 13

While Charlotte couldn't find a breakthrough during their 0-0 home draw with Houston, Allan Saint-Maximin looked like the best player on the field. Dean Smith's new left winger was at the center of nearly every threatening move and has the look of an MLS star.

12. Real Salt Lake
Previous ranking: 12

Still winless in league play since May, RSL drew 2-2 with LAFC on Saturday. They created a slew of quality chances, but also proved too open in defensive transition as control and tactical balance still eludes them.

13. Orlando City
Previous ranking: 16

Antoine Griezmann continued his absolute tear with the lone goal in Orlando's 1-0 win over San Diego. Now with eight goal contributions in eight games since debuting for the Lions, Griezmann has quickly turned around Orlando's season: they're now above the playoff line in the East.

14. FC Dallas
Previous ranking: 14

If there's a debate about MLS's best striker, Petar Musa is doing his best to end it. The Croatia international managed two goals, including the game winner, and an assist in Dallas' 4-3 win over Kansas City. While the home side's focus lacked, Musa's certainly didn't.

15. Philadelphia Union
Previous ranking: 15

Since league play resumed after the World Cup, the Union are yet to lose. Saturday's 2-0 victory over Montréal lengthened that streak of results to eight games, with six of them going down as wins. With yet another goal from Cavan Sullivan, Philadelphia are flying.

16. San Diego FC
Previous ranking: 15

Missing star midfielder Jeppe Tverskov due to a card suspension, San Diego's ball progression never turned into regular chances in a 1-0 road loss to Orlando. Without the Dane, the sophomore side simply can't carry the same threat going forward.

17. Minnesota United
Previous ranking: 11

For a team that prides itself on effective defending, conceding three goals in the first half in a 5-4 loss to the Timbers was nowhere near good enough for Minnesota. Still, breakout striker Marcus Caldeira's brace could signal longer-term attacking improvement for a team fighting for a playoff spot.

18. LA Galaxy
Previous ranking: 20

The Galaxy marked Sergi Roberto's first MLS start with a 2-1 victory over New England. The former Barcelona man was a touch magnet in central midfield, helping his new team conduct play. If Roberto and Chucky Lozano, who notched an assist, maintain this form, the Galaxy won't be easily dismissed.

19. Toronto FC
Previous ranking: 22

Josh Sargent appears to be finding his form in MLS. While the U.S. striker had a quiet start to life in Toronto, he notched a hat trick in a 4-4 draw with Chicago over the weekend. It was a top-tier showing from Sargent atop Robin Fraser's attacking structure that led to a point for the hosts.

20. Red Bull New York
Previous ranking: 19

Now below the playoff line out East following a 0-0 draw in Seattle, that Red Bull New York didn't do more in the summer transfer window is a major concern. Without any game-changing additions made to the squad before deadline day, it's difficult to see how Michael Bradley's team will rebound.

21. Seattle Sounders
Previous ranking: 21

On Saturday, Sounders fans could breathe a collective sigh of relief upon seeing Cristian Roldan make his first start for the team since May. Still, the USMNT midfielder's return wasn't enough to see Seattle claim their first win in months. A 0-0 draw with the Red Bulls had to suffice.

22. Portland Timbers
Previous ranking: 23

With star striker Kevin Kelsy now off to Rangers in the Scottish Premiership, replacement Vincent Janssen didn't waste any time filling the Venezuelan's shoes. Janssen notched a hat trick in the Timbers' wild 5-4 home win over Minnesota.

23. San Jose Earthquakes
Previous ranking: 18

It looked as if the Quakes' winless run, one that stretches all the way back to May, was going to come to an end on Saturday. That is, until Austin managed a 97th-minute equalizer and a victory turned into a 1-1 draw for San Jose. The Earthquakes are in a bad, bad place.

24. D.C. United
Previous ranking: 24

D.C.'s meeting with Cincinnati was postponed due to weather, leaving the club without a chance to break a five-game winless streak.

25. Austin FC
Previous ranking: 25

Thanks to an equalizer from Guilherme Biro deep in second-half stoppage time, Austin secured a 1-1 draw against San Jose. The result marked four straight games without a loss in league play for the Texas capital club.

26. Columbus Crew
Previous ranking: 27

It didn't take Santi Rodriguez long to open his account in Columbus. The former New York City star bagged the opening goal for the Crew in a 3-0 victory over Colorado. With a remade attack, could this team make a late push for a spot in the postseason?

27. Colorado Rapids
Previous ranking: 26

After trading Navarro to St. Louis and adding new pieces to the attack just before deadline day, the Rapids were nowhere near full strength in a 3-0 loss to the Crew. Colorado will have to wait for their new pieces to arrive and integrate to reach their full potential.

28. Atlanta United
Previous ranking: 28

At last, there are signs of life in Atlanta. During their 2-2 draw with Miami, new striker Breel Embolo made his debut and scored a late equalizer from the spot. Elsewhere, young defensive midfielder Mauricio Amaro made his first MLS appearance and looked extremely comfortable amid his new surroundings.

29. CF Montréal
Previous ranking: 29

Back to the bottom of the East after falling 2-0 in Philadelphia, it's difficult to see Montréal climbing the standings anytime soon. Even with Alexis Sánchez in the lineup, this team is still light on talent.

30. Sporting Kansas City
Previous ranking: 30

Although they managed one of their best attacking outings of the year, spurred on by new winger André Luiz's first start, Kansas City couldn't hold on for a point in Dallas. They fell 4-3 thanks to a late penalty by Musa.

stories.headline: Money isn't everything: Penrith star's big future hint
stories.summary: Penrith star Liam Martin has revealed he could forego more money elsewhere to stay at the Panthers, as he weighs up his future beyond the end of 2027.
stories.body:
Liam Martin has given the first real indication he could refuse more money elsewhere to stay at Penrith, declaring the dollar-figure on his NRL contract won't be the only deciding factor in his future.

Martin has put contract talks with the Panthers on hold until after the end of the season, with the focus now clearly on Sunday's qualifying final against Sydney Roosters.

The Panthers have a number of stars off contract at the end of next season, with Nathan Cleary and Isaah Yeo's future also yet to be locked in beyond 2027.

Moses Leota is another star off contract, with the prop forward also indicating on Tuesday he would find it hard to leave the foot of the mountains.

But the sheer number of big names off contract has left Penrith in a difficult position, juggling several offers under the salary while trying to retain all talent.

If Martin remains unsigned by November 1, the Kangaroos Test forward would likely command more money on the open market.

The tax-free money from PNG would also loom as an option, given the NRL has not allowed the Chiefs to sign Hudson Young for their initial offer of $900,000 a season after Canberra offered him $1.1 million to stay.

But Martin made clear money would not be the only thing he would consider, and there was a real appeal to staying at Penrith.

"There could be more money elsewhere, but money is not everything at the end of the day," Martin said.

"I have a great bunch of mates here, best mates who I have been with since I was 18.

"I have been in Penrith for 10 years now and have a little boy. There is a lot to weigh up, it's not an easy decision. It's one I'll have to make in due time."

Since Penrith's run began in 2021, they have lost more than half of their first title-winning team to rival clubs.

Until this point none of Penrith's home-grown talent have lined up against them in a grand final, with the likes of Apisai Koroisau and Jarome Luai yet to play finals at Wests Tigers.

"There's a duality to it," Martin said.

"I couldn't imagine going somewhere and experiencing failure and just how tough it would be.

"But also the challenge of building a successful club somewhere else, I feel like I could offer something. It's a tough decision.

"That success is so addictive, and what we've got here is an incredible culture."

Penrith have already lost Brian To'o to the Chiefs for 2028, while Yeo is edging closer to formalising a new deal.

The Panthers also remain confident they can keep Cleary, who has not put a timeline on his decision.

Leota, meanwhile, is expected to stay, but said he was unsure if a deal would be done by November 1.

"Penrith is my home and this is all I have ever known," Leota said on Tuesday.

"It would be hard to get me away from here, but we'll see what happens."
